la:other:Fannius.html:
Fannĭus, a,
the name of a Roman gens: 1. C. Fannius Strabo, son-in-law of Laelius, introduced as a speaker by Cicero in de Rep. and Lael.; 2. His son of the same name, who was consul A. U.C. 632, ; ; . C. Fannius, an historian, contemporary with Pliny the younger, —
Derivv.
Fannĭus, a, um, adj., of or belonging to Fannius, Fannian: lex, a sumptuary law introduced by the consul C. Fannius, ; .—
Fannĭānus, a, um, adj., the same: conturbat me epitome Bruti Fanniana, Orell. N. cr.: charta, manufactured in the establishment of Q. Rhemnius Fannius, , §§ 75, 78.

la:noun:fanum.gloss: shrine, temple, sanctuary, place dedicated to a deity
senses: shrine, temple, sanctuary, place dedicated to a deity
as a declinable word to introduce a placename named after a Saint, e.g. Fanum Sancti Iohannis for the various places named Saint John('s), San Juan, etc.
la:noun:fanum.html:
fānum, i, n.
fari; cf. Müll.; Paul. ex , and 93, 17 Müll.;
,
a place dedicated to some deity by forms of consecration, a sanctuary, temple (syn.: templum, aedes, delubrum, cella, sacellum, sacrarium): in ea pugna Jovis Statoris aedem votam, ut Romulus ante voverat: sed fa num tantum, id est locus templo effatus, sacratus fuerat,; : eamque unam ob causam Xerxes inflammari Atheniensium fana jussisse dicitur, quod deos inclusos parietibus contineri nefas esse duceret,: pro patriis fanis atque delubris propugnandum,: de aris ac focis, de fanis ac templis,: fana templaque expilavit,: propter fani religionem,: fanum antiquissimum et sanctissimum,: Dianae Ephesi,: Junonis,: Herculis,: Hammonis,: Eumenidum,;

la:adj:fanaticus.html:
fānātĭcus, a, um, adj.
1. fanum
.
Pertaining to a temple: PECVNIA, Inscr. Veron. ap. Bull. Dell' ; cf. Borghesi, ib.—
Inspired by a divinity, enthusiastic.
Lit.: ut fanaticus, oestro Percussus, Bellona, tuo,; so cf the priests of Bellona,: jam subeuntibus armatis muros fanatici Galli ... occurrunt,; of the priests of Cybele,; Prud. στεφ. 10, 1061, cf. also: Galli vaticinantes fanatico carmine,: si servus inter fanaticos non semper caput jactaret, etc. (shortly after: circa fana bacchatus),: fanatica dicitur arbor fulmine icta, Paul. ex Müll.—
Transf., frantic, furious, mad: isti philosophi superstitiosi et paene fanatici,: cursus,: jactatio corporis,: error,: furor, et saep.: jactare id (caput) et comas excutientem rotare, fanaticum est,.—* Adv.: fānātĭce, franticly, madly: absonis ululatibus constrepentes fanatice pervolant,.
